resources.string: The M1 Abrams is an American main battle tank, developed in the 1970s. It entered service in 1980. The first models of the M1 Abrams were equipped with a 105 mm M68 gun. Starting with the M1A1 version, it is armed with the 120 mm M256 gun. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.
The C1 Ariete is an Italian main battle tank, developed in the 1980s-1990s. It entered service in 1995. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine guns: 12.7 mm, 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The Challenger 1 is a British main battle tank, developed in the 1980s. It entered service in 1983. The modernization of the Challenger 1 gave birth to the Challenger 2, which entered service in 1998. In the United Kingdom, the Challenger 1 was retired from service with the arrival of the Challenger 2. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The Challenger 2 is a British main battle tank, developed in the 1990s. It entered service in 1998. Known as FV4030, it is the main battle tank of the British Army. It participated in engagements in Kosovo and Iraq. Exported to Oman in 38 units. In 2021, the British Army announced the modernization of 148 tanks under the designation Challenger 3. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The Chieftain is a British main battle tank, developed in the 1950s-1960s by Leyland Motors. It entered service in 1966. It underwent several modernization campaigns up to the Chieftain Mk-11 version. Employed in British armored units until its replacement by the Challenger 1 in 1983. Exported to Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Jordan (under the designation Khalid) and Oman (under the designation Shir). Versions: Chieftain Mk.1 (1966), Chieftain Mk.5 (1972), Khalid, Shir. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The Leopard 2 is a German main battle tank, developed in the 1970s. Versions: Leopard 2A0 (1979), Leopard 2A1 (1982), Leopard 2A2 (1983), Leopard 2A3 (1984), Leopard 2A4 (1985), Leopard 2A5 (2000), Leopard 2A6 (2001), Leopard 2A7 (2014), Leopard 2A7V (2021), Leopard 2A8 (2023). Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The Leopard 1 is a German main battle tank, developed in the 1950s-1960s. It entered service in 1965. Widely exported, it is currently in service in Turkey, Brazil and Chile. Since February 2023, Germany has been delivering Leopard 1 tanks to Ukraine. The Leopard 1 chassis served as the basis for various support vehicles. Versions: Leopard 1A1, 1A1A1, 1A2, 1A3, 1A4, 1A5. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 4.

The T-55 is a Russian main battle tank, developed in the Soviet Union in the 1950s. It entered service in 1958. Very widely distributed, it was produced under license in Poland, Czechoslovakia and Romania. It participated in numerous conflicts and remains in service in several armed forces. Versions: T-55K, T-55A, T-55AK, T-55AM. Main gun: 100 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.

The M60 is an American main battle tank, developed in the 1950s. Very widely exported, it remains in service in several armed forces. It underwent several modernization campaigns: M60A1 (1962), M60A2 (1970), M60A3 (1975). Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm Browning M2. Crew: 4.

The Magach tanks are versions adapted to Israeli needs of the American M48 and M60 tanks. Versions: Magach 5, Magach 6B Gal Batash, Magach 6M Tadach, Magach 7A, Magach 7C. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine guns: 7.62 mm, 12.7 mm Browning. Crew: 4.

The Merkava Mk IV is an Israeli main battle tank, developed in the 1990s. It entered service in 2004. Its chassis served as the basis for the Namer heavy armored personnel carrier. Israel is the sole user of the Merkava Mk IV. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine guns: 7.62 mm, 12.7 mm. Mortar: 60 mm. Crew: 4.
The T-62 is a Soviet medium tank, which entered service in 1961. Main gun: 115 mm. Crew: 4 (tank commander, turret operator, loader, driver).

The T-64 is a Soviet main battle tank, developed in the 1960s. It entered service in 1965. First Soviet tank to integrate automatic loading. Versions: T-64A, T-64B, T-64BM Bulat. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Anti-tank missile: AT-8 (T-64B). Crew: 3.

The T-64 is a Soviet main battle tank, developed in the 1960s. It entered service in 1965. First Soviet tank to integrate automatic loading. Versions: T-64A, T-64B, T-64BM Bulat. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Anti-tank missile: AT-8 (T-64B). Crew: 3.

The T-72 is a Russian main battle tank, developed in the 1960s-1970s. It entered service in 1973. Versions: T-72, T-72K, T-72A, T-72M, T-72AV, T-72B, T-72B1, T-72BK, T-72C, T-72BM, T-72B3. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.
The T-80 is a Russian main battle tank, developed in the 1980s. Versions: T-80U, T-80UK, T-80UD, T-80UE-1. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.
The T-90 is a Russian main battle tank, developed in the 1990s. It entered service in 1992. Versions: T-90A, T-90M, T-90MS. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.

The AMX-30 is a French main battle tank, developed in the 1960s. It entered service in 1967. Nearly 3,500 AMX-30 tanks were produced for the French army and for export. Replaced by the Leclerc tank in the French army. Versions: AMX-30B (1967), AMX-30B2 (1980). Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm ANF1. Crew: 4.
The Arjun is an Indian main battle tank, developed in the 1990s-2000s. It entered service in 2004. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.

The K1 is a South Korean main battle tank, developed in the 1970s-1980s by Hyundai (now Rotem) with technical assistance from General Dynamics. It entered service in 1987. Known under the designations Type 88 and 88-Tank, it was developed to counter North Korean T-62 tanks. Its production was replaced by the K2 Black Panther from 2014. Versions: K1/Type 88/88-Tank (1987), K1A1 (2001), K1A2 (2013). Main gun: 105 mm (K1), 120 mm (K1A1). Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.
The Merkava Mk 3 is an Israeli main battle tank, which entered service in 1990. Main gun: 120 mm MG251 (smoothbore). Machine guns: three 7.62 mm MAG. Crew: 4 (tank commander, driver, gunner, loader).

The PT-91 Twardy is a Polish main battle tank, developed in the 1990s by Bumar Labedy based on the T-72M1. It entered service in 1995. Produced in 232 units for the Polish army and exported to Malaysia (48 units under the name PT-91M Pendekar, 2007-2010). Main gun: 125 mm. Machine guns: 7.62 mm (coaxial), 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.

The Type 10 is a Japanese main battle tank, developed in the 2000s by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. It entered service in 2012. Main gun: 120 mm (44 calibers, 36 rounds). Machine guns: 7.62 mm (coaxial), 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.

The Type 98 (ZTZ-98) is a Chinese main battle tank, introduced in 1999 during a military parade in Beijing. Resembling the T-72, it is distinguished by a welded turret. Main gun: 125 mm (smoothbore). Crew: 3.

The ZTZ-99 (Type 99) is a Chinese main battle tank, developed in the 1990s-2000s. It entered service in 2003. Equipped with a thermal camera, a stabilized panoramic sight with hunter-killer capability and an all-around laser countermeasures system. Versions: ZTZ-99G, ZTZ-99A1, ZTZ-99A2. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.

The Merkava Mk 1 is an Israeli main battle tank, delivered to the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) from 1979. Superior to the Syrian T-72. Versions: Merkava 1, Merkava 1B. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm (coaxial). Crew: 4.
The AMX-13 is a French light tank, produced between 1953 and 1985. Main gun: 105 mm (self-propelled). Crew: 3.
The K2 Black Panther is a South Korean main battle tank, developed in the 2000s. It entered service in 2014. Main gun: 120 mm (55 calibers). Crew: 3.

The Leclerc is a French main battle tank, developed in the 1980s. It entered service in 1991. It replaced the AMX-30 tanks in French armored units. 388 units were delivered to the United Arab Emirates between 2000 and 2003. Deployed in Kosovo and Lebanon. Main gun: 120 mm. Machine guns: 12.7 mm (coaxial), 7.62 mm. Crew: 3.

The TR-85, Tanc Românesc model 1985, is a Romanian main battle tank, developed in the 1980s. It entered service in 1986. Developed from the TR-580, an elongated version of the T-55, it is used exclusively by Romania. Versions: TR-85, TR-85M1 Bizonul. Main gun: 100 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.
The VT-4 (MBT-3000) is a Chinese main battle tank, presented in 2012. In 2016, the Thai army acquired 28 VT-4 tanks. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 3.

The EBRC Jaguar, Engin Blindé de Reconnaissance et de Combat (Armored Reconnaissance and Combat Vehicle), is a French 6×6 wheeled armored fighting vehicle, developed in the 2010s. It entered service in 2022. Intended to replace the AMX-10RCR. Main gun: 40 mm. Machine gun: 7.62 mm. Crew: 3.

The Stridsvagn 103 (Strv 103) is a Swedish main battle tank, developed in the 1950s. Perfectly amphibious with a flotation skirt installable in 20 minutes, it is propelled in water by its tracks at 6 km/h. Versions: Strv 103A, 103B, 103C, 103D. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine guns: two 7.62 mm. Crew: 3.

The T-14 Armata is a Russian main battle tank, in development since the 2010s. Serial production was announced for 2019. Equipped with an unmanned remotely operated turret with ammunition stored in an automatic loader. The three crew members are located in the front of the chassis. Main gun: 125 mm. Machine guns: 12.7 mm or 7.62 mm. Crew: 3.

The Type 16 MCV, Maneuver Combat Vehicle, is a Japanese 8×8 wheeled light tank, developed in the 2010s. It entered service in 2016. Armed with a 105 mm stabilized manually loaded gun, with the powertrain at the front left and the driver on the right. Can receive additional armor. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.

The ZTL-11 is a Chinese 8×8 wheeled light tank, developed in the 2010s. It entered service in 2014. Based on the ZBL-09 chassis, it includes a weapon stabilizer and a thermal camera. The 105 mm gun can fire explosive, shaped charge and sub-caliber anti-tank shells. Main gun: 105 mm. Machine gun: 12.7 mm. Crew: 4.
